per_design.label: prompted instructed lying (the design this paper audits)
per_design.n_rollouts_note: the file is aggregated to one lying rate per dataset x instruction; no rollout, prompt or response text is released in it
per_design.item_key: dataset name (the only key in the file); no question-, prompt- or rollout-level key exists

deception_value.determined_by: the instruction column the rate is tabulated under

i: the 26 instruction texts are the column keys: the contrast *is* the prompt change, so no two contrasted cells share a prompt hash
ii: the tabulated value is the rate of lying under a named lie instruction; D is the generating condition, which fails (ii) by definition
iii: the file is aggregated to rates; with no question-level key released, whether any one item was realized under both outcomes cannot be read off it either way
iv: no prompt or response text is released in this file, so what a black-box detector would read cannot be checked here
v: D is definitionally the instruction that produced the response

per_design.detector_contrast_note: PREREG_EXP_XP.md §5: a detector contrast is run only when all five predicates are True, so no accuracy is computed or reported here.

per_design.label: instrumental, goal-directed deception, un-instructed (the `instrumental_lying_df_*` files)
per_design.item_key: sha256 of the whole released prompt

deception_value.determined_by: the generating condition: `label` equals the row's index parity in every row of every file, so it is recoverable without reading any text

supplementary_adjacent_pair_key.note: the release has no scenario-id field; this key is ours, and every number under it is supplementary
the release has no scenario-id field; this key is ours, and every number under it is supplementary
the release has no scenario-id field; this key is ours, and every number under it is supplementary

i: 138 distinct whole-prompt hashes across the contrasted cells where (i) requires one; the deceptive and honest cells differ in the prompt by construction, and 0 of the supplementary scenario pairs have a byte-identical prompt
ii: `label` equals the row's index parity in every row of all three files, so it is a deterministic function of the generating condition, not an off-label grade
iii: under the only released item key (whole-prompt sha256) 0 items carry both outcomes; the supplementary pair key does reach both outcomes, but only across two different prompts, which is what (i) forbids
iv: the released channel is the transcript plus elicitation logprob differences: no scratchpad, no training metadata, and no generating-condition field inside the text a detector would read
v: `label` is a property of which prompt variant produced the rollout, so it is definitionally equivalent to the process that produced the detector's input

per_design.item_key: sha256 of the whole released prompt

single_condition_prompts.note: prompts appearing in one file only are follow-up turns that embed the previous answer, so they cannot be byte-identical across conditions; the first-turn prompts are the ones that are

deception_value.field: which file the row came from

min_cell_size_gate.note: PREREG_EXP_XA.md §6's floor, adopted by reference; reported because this design clears it, not because a contrast is run -- §5 forbids that while any predicate is False

i: 1109 prompts are byte-identical across the two conditions, hashed over the whole prompt and not over a system message
ii: D is which file the row came from, i.e. the fine-tuning target: a deterministic function of the generating condition, which (ii) excludes however accurate it is
iii: 1109 items are realized under both values of D, and 1109 of them have differing completion sets, so the contrast can be taken within an item
iv: the released fields are a bare `User: ... Assistant:` prompt and the completion: no instruction, no scratchpad, no training metadata in the text
v: D is definitionally the objective the model was fine-tuned on, so it is equivalent to the process that produced the detector's input
